provenance.note: Blinded single-subagent adjudication (MERGE-PLAN §2): vendor labels stripped, A/B randomized per file, candidate-pair focus. confirmed_delta promoted only after caller original-span confirmation.

base_member_text: No iteration cap exists; non-convergence would loop forever (L8-L15).
audit_member_text: There is no maximum iteration count at L8-L15, so a finite but nonconvergent/oscillatory input can loop indefinitely.

base_member_text: The elementwise operators (.* ./) suggest vector omega/h support ('omvec'), but k*h uses the plain * operator (L9-L10), which is only elementwise for scalar h or scalar k; for vector h and vector k of the same orientation it still works elementwise only when one is scalar — a latent shape restriction not documented.
audit_member_text: Vector interface mismatch across L3 and L9-L10: some omega operations are elementwise, but multiplication by h uses matrix '*' and error is initially sized from length(h) at L7. The routine works for the scalar h used by its neighboring caller, but general h/omega vectors can have incompatible dimensions or unintended matrix products.

base_member_text: constants and params_defined are empty because the only numeric literal is the convergence tolerance .000001 embedded in the while condition (L8), which has no name in the file; per A-2 it is preserved in the verbatim span of L8.

audit_member_text: Singularity/termination defect for omega=0 across L3 and L8-L13: the initial expression is 0/sqrt(tanh(0)) and yields NaN; after one Newton pass the NaN relative error makes the comparison error>1e-6 false, so the loop exits and returns NaN rather than detecting the singular input or converging to k=0.

The Newton step divides by fp at L11 and the convergence metric divides by k at L12 without zero/finite checks. NaN comparisons can terminate the loop as if converged, while Inf/finite failures are not reported.
The local variable error at L7 and L12 shadows MATLAB's built-in error function, preventing diagnostic use of error by name within this scope.
